A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SWE-Bench Pro, with the same benchmark, curation framework, and identifiable main-text and appendix material. The text, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations on the public and commercial sets, performance breakdowns, and trajectory failure analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports original model evaluations and failure analyses, plus a new experiment removing requirements and interface information.

M1.justification: The benchmark-construction workflow, augmented task format, SWE-Agent scaffold, and GPT-5 failure-classification procedure remain substantively unchanged. The new augmentation ablation tests existing components without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: The 731 public, 276 commercial, and 858 held-out problems retain their repository and language coverage. Section 6.2 adds evaluation with problem statements alone, introducing a more ambiguous input scenario without requirements or interface specifications.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the evaluated model panel: Table 1 adds Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Kimi K2 Instruct, and GPT-OSS 120B; Table 5 additionally reports GPT-OSS 20B. Earlier public-set comparators remain represented in Table 5. Commercial Table 2 adds GPT-5 high alongside the earlier score now labeled medium.

E3.justification: Section 5 changes the stated maximum from 200 to 50 agent turns. V2 also introduces the controlled augmentation-removal evaluation and distinguishes GPT-5 reasoning configurations. These are substantial reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 6.2 and Table 3 add a focused two-model ablation testing dependence on requirements and interface specifications. The failure breakdown is revised, but its classification procedure is retained. The existing complexity, language, and repository analyses remain, including the identical plot renumbered from Figure 4 to Figure 3.

E5.justification: V1 Section 3.2 specifies three repetitions of each test suite to filter flaky tests; v2 removes this exact count, retaining only 'several times' in Section 4.3. This reduces repetition reporting without establishing fewer runs. Neither version reports model-evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The headline public comparison changes from GPT-5 leading at 23.3% to Sonnet 4.5 at 43.6%, while earlier scores remain in v2 Table 5 under explicitly capped settings. New ablation results are 25.9% versus 8.40% for GPT-5 high and 22.7% versus 8.20% for Opus 4.1. Commercial Table 2 adds GPT-5 high at 15.7%, and many failure counts change. These are added or revised results, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The added failure-category descriptions are explanatory definitions rather than mathematical developments.

C1.justification: The benchmark's central contributions remain unchanged. The abstract revises the performance ceiling from below 25%, with GPT-5 best at 23.3%, to below 45%; the introduction removes its explicit 6–12-month saturation forecast. The conclusion nevertheless retains the earlier approximately 23% characterization.

C2.justification: V2 adds a model-capacity interpretation of the retained complexity plot and interprets the augmentation ablation through verifier false negatives. It removes the explicit limitations concerning restricted issue scope and overly prescriptive augmentation, although related ambiguity caveats remain elsewhere.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies the $2 analysis cap, identifies the default SWE-Agent prompt, states that Opus 4.1 uses no extended thinking, and expands failure-category descriptions. It removes detailed repository-sourcing and commit-validation explanations. Hardware, container information, access links, and the substantive judge prompt remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work coverage is substantially narrowed by removing discussions and references for CrossCodeEval, RepoBench, BigCodeBench, SWE-perf, OpenHands, AgentCoder, and CodeAct. This removes whole strands of benchmark and agent-architecture context, while retaining the core novelty positioning around contamination-resistant enterprise tasks.

P1.justification: V2 substantially condenses the introduction, related work, sourcing discussion, and limitations, and removes acknowledgments. It reorganizes the analysis around a new ablation subsection and inserts a failure-category appendix before the retained examples and judge prompt. The author list also expands.

P2.justification: V2 removes the overview Figure 1 and rebuilds v1 Figure 2 without its model-performance comparison panel, rearranging the retained distributions. It adds the ablation table and an expanded appendix display of earlier public results. Other plots are unchanged apart from relocation and numbering. Appendix formatting introduces clipped category labels and visible escape characters in examples.

improvement.justification: The new augmentation ablation and clearer evaluation disclosures improve support and interpretability. However, the updated headline results are not reconciled with the retained 23% conclusion, and failure-analysis prose becomes inconsistent: Opus's quoted 35.9% matched v1, but v2's counts imply 37.3%. Relevant limitations are also removed, and appendix formatting deteriorates. These material benefits and harms leave the net quality direction unclear.
